# SparseGF2

> Fast stabilizer (Clifford) circuit simulator for monitored random Clifford circuits:
> measurement-induced and purification transitions, dynamically generated codes, erasure
> protection of those codes. Reads Stim's circuit language; verified against Stim. Python
> package `sparsegf2`, CLI `sparsegf2`, MCP server `sparsegf2-mcp`.

Agents should use the MCP server (`claude mcp add sparsegf2 -- sparsegf2-mcp`) or
`sparsegf2 <command> --json`. Every result is a compact JSON summary (under about 8000
characters); pass `output_dir` to save full arrays. Seeds are ints; qubit lists are
`[0, 1]` or `"0:2"`; system qubits are 0..n-1 and reference qubits follow.

Ensembles: a graph collection (`"realizations": G` in the JSON graph, or a list of graphs
in Python) runs `circuits_per_graph` random circuits per graph (default 1); trajectory t
uses graph t // circuits_per_graph, and `trajectories` may be omitted to run all of them.
Every probe accepts its own `checkpoints`. Erasure protection of the generated code (each
qubit erased independently with probability e after the circuit): probes
`erasure_first_failure` (first-failure sizes over random orderings) and
`uncorrectable_region_counts` (exact counts for small erasures), `code_snapshot` to save
the code; `sparsegf2.analysis.erasure_failure_probability` gives
Phi(e) = sum_m C(n,m) e^m (1-e)^(n-m) P_C(m) and `erasure_tolerance` gives e_delta.

## Docs

- [docs/GETTING_STARTED.md](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md): full getting-started guide for people: install, concepts (pictures, layers, checkpoints, probes, seeds, graph collections), a first erasure study end to end, scaling up (estimates, chunks, SLURM), troubleshooting
- [docs/MCP_GETTING_STARTED.md](docs/MCP_GETTING_STARTED.md): setting up the MCP server: install, connecting Claude Code, Claude Desktop or other clients, a worked first session, background jobs, troubleshooting
- [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md): how the simulator works inside (column-major tableau, reference rows, ensemble engine, randomness contract, erasure kernels), with diagrams
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): install, which entry point to use, five-minute tour, conventions, pitfalls
- [docs/LLM_INTERFACE.md](docs/LLM_INTERFACE.md): full CLI and MCP reference with examples and client registration
- [README.md](README.md): install, the Python library tour (including the erasure workflow), performance
- [docs/LITERATURE.md](docs/LITERATURE.md): the observables the monitored-circuit literature uses and how they are computed
- [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md): architecture, data layout and benchmarks

## Code

- [src/sparsegf2/api.py](src/sparsegf2/api.py): JSON service layer (capabilities, inspect_circuit, run_circuit, run_ensemble, estimate_ensemble, start_ensemble_job, job_status, cancel_job, list_jobs, load_results, sample_erasure_regions, erasure_curves)
- [src/sparsegf2/mipt.py](src/sparsegf2/mipt.py): MonitoredCircuit protocol (graph collections, circuits_per_graph), probes with their own checkpoints, EnsembleResult (values, layers, graph_index, snapshots, code)
- [src/sparsegf2/codes.py](src/sparsegf2/codes.py): StabilizerCode, a code from generators, Pauli strings or a saved snapshot: lost information l(A) = I(A:R), first-failure sizes, exhaustive uncorrectable counts
- [src/sparsegf2/analysis.py](src/sparsegf2/analysis.py): failure_by_size, exact_failure_by_size, erasure_failure_probability (hybrid exact/sampled), erasure_tolerance, Kaplan-Meier survival, mean_and_error
- [src/sparsegf2/observables.py](src/sparsegf2/observables.py): entropies, code dimension, erasure statistics, contiguous distance on a Simulator state
- [src/sparsegf2/simulator.py](src/sparsegf2/simulator.py): Simulator (stim.TableauSimulator-style API)
- [src/sparsegf2/circuit.py](src/sparsegf2/circuit.py): Circuit (Stim syntax, CLIFFORD_1Q/2Q extensions)
- [examples/](examples/): complete study scripts (purification time on a Watts-Strogatz graph collection, transition scans, erasure protection of the generated code vs depth)
